title: NumPy Random Permutations and Shuffling
learningObjectives: Explain the concepts behind numpy random permutations and shuffling.
Choose an appropriate NumPy random generator method and its parameters.
Use seeded generators for reproducible examples and tests.
Validate sample shape, range and data type.
Describe the assumptions and limitations of a finite random sample.

understand.concept: A permutation rearranges the order of elements. Generator.permutation returns a permuted copy for an array, while Generator.shuffle rearranges an array in place. Sampling without replacement selects distinct population members when the requested sample size does not exceed the population.
understand.whyItMatters: Permutation and shuffling support randomized ordering, dataset splitting, simulations and unbiased presentation of examples.
understand.analogy: A random generator is like a repeatable deck-shuffling machine: a starting seed and the sequence of operations determine the generated sequence.
understand.summary: A permutation rearranges the order of elements. Generator.permutation returns a permuted copy for an array, while Generator.shuffle rearranges an array in place. Sampling without replacement selects distinct population members when the requested sample size does not exceed the population.

explain.narrative: Run the examples and inspect the sample properties. A random sample is not a promise of exact theoretical frequencies; tests should focus on stable properties such as shape, valid range and reproducibility. examples.title: Create a permutation
examples.code:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(12)
x = rng.permutation(np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5]))
print(sorted(x.tolist()))
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create a permutation with a seeded NumPy random generator so the validation is deterministic.

examples.title: Shuffle an array in place
examples.code:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(12)
x = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
rng.shuffle(x)
print(sorted(x.tolist()))
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates shuffle an array in place with a seeded NumPy random generator so the validation is deterministic.

examples.title: Permute row positions
examples.code:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
a = np.array([[1, 10], [2, 20], [3, 30]])
p = rng.permutation(a, axis=0)
print(p.shape, sorted(p[:, 0].tolist()))
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates permute row positions with a seeded NumPy random generator so the validation is deterministic.

examples.title: Sample without replacement
examples.code:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(9)
s = rng.choice(20, size=6, replace=False)
print(len(s), len(np.unique(s)))
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates sample without replacement with a seeded NumPy random generator so the validation is deterministic.

examples.title: Keep original order when permuting a copy
examples.code:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(4)
a = np.arange(6)
b = rng.permutation(a)
print(a.tolist(), sorted(b.tolist()))
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates keep original order when permuting a copy with a seeded NumPy random generator so the validation is deterministic.

questions.prompt: What does a seeded NumPy Generator provide?
questions.answer: A reproducible pseudo-random sequence when the generator and call sequence are the same.
options: A truly random sequence that can never repeat.
A reproducible pseudo-random sequence when the generator and call sequence are the same.
A guarantee of exact theoretical frequencies.
A generator that ignores its parameters.
questions.explanation: A seed initializes a deterministic pseudo-random process.

questions.prompt: Why should distribution parameters be chosen carefully?
questions.answer: They encode the assumptions and scale of the model.
options: They encode the assumptions and scale of the model.
They only change the printed format.
They guarantee a fixed sample mean.
They remove the need to validate data.
questions.explanation: Parameters define the distribution being modeled.

questions.prompt: Which check is generally robust for a generated sample?
questions.answer: Check its shape and valid range.
options: Require the sample mean to equal the theoretical mean exactly.
Check its shape and valid range.
Assume every generated value is unique.
Expect the same values from different seeds.
questions.explanation: Shape and support constraints are stable properties.

questions.prompt: What does sampling without replacement mean?
questions.answer: The same population item cannot be selected more than once in that sample.
options: The same population item cannot be selected more than once in that sample.
Every possible item must be selected.
The sample must be sorted.
The generator cannot use a seed.
questions.explanation: Without replacement, selected population members are not repeated.

questions.prompt: What is an important limitation of a finite random sample?
questions.answer: Observed frequencies and statistics can differ from theoretical values.
options: It always contains invalid values.
Observed frequencies and statistics can differ from theoretical values.
It cannot be reproduced with a seed.
It must have a normal distribution.
questions.explanation: Finite samples naturally vary around theoretical expectations.
